questions.explanation: Cross-multiplication gives $a/b=c/d$ exactly when $ad=bc$, provided both denominators are nonzero. Equal numerators or equal denominators alone are insufficient.

Equal denominators do not help when numerators differ, as in $1/5\neq2/5$.

options: They are undefined despite nonzero denominators.
questions.explanation: The cross-products are $2\cdot6=12$ and $3\cdot4=12$. Since they are equal and both denominators are nonzero, $2/3=4/6$.
questions.source_support: Two fractions $a/b$ and $c/d$ are equal exactly when $ad=bc$.

questions.question: Why does a rational representation $a/b$ require $b\neq0$?
options: Because every numerator must be zero.
questions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined: no number can serve as a quotient that reverses multiplication by zero. Therefore a rational representation must have a nonzero denominator.
questions.source_support: A rational number has the form $a/b$ with $b\neq0$.
